messages:
simon: Quick flag  production alarms showing a small but steady rise in 'parse_error: missing_envelope' after yesterday's 'envelope' change to streaming output. Seen across a few customers and internal sidecars.
anya: Which shapes are failing? Is this the old newline-delimited-token clients?
jeff: Confirmed: legacy clients expect raw token frames (newline delimited strings). New runtime wraps each frame in {\"envelope\": {meta...}, \"payload\": ...}. Parsers that stream-scan for newlines are choking.
simon: Important: the envelope was added to carry per-chunk model-info and token-score telemetry without breaking the token stream for modern SDKs. But some edge proxies and small-device clients can't be updated quickly.
chloe: Short-term options I see: (A) edge translator that unwraps envelope into legacy raw frames for detected legacy clients; (B) runtime emits legacy shape when client sends `x-rw-compat: legacy`; (C) dual-write: emit both envelope and legacy frames (would double bandwidth).
jeff: Bandwidth doubling is unsafe for mobile clients. Runtime toggles require opt-in from client; won't help devices that can't be changed. Edge translator seems practical.
anya: Edge translator concerns: it touches the egress path and must preserve stream order and any timing metadata used by batching. Also must maintain identical cache keys for prefix caching: unwrapped bytes must match previous raw output.
simon: Agreed. Also security: don't accidentally remove security headers accidentally embedded in envelope.meta. Need strict allowlist of meta fields safe to drop for legacy clients.
chloe: Proposed detection heuristic at edge: on connection start, peek at first N bytes. If JSON envelope detected and user-agent in legacy-list OR UA unknown AND size < 1MB (likely IoT), then enable 'legacy-unwrap' for that connection and increment metric `compat_unwrap_v1`. Fallback to pass-through for others.
jeff: Pseudocode for egress translator:
```
on_connect(conn):
  buf = peek(conn, 512)
  if looks_like_envelope(buf) and client_in_legacy_bucket(conn.ua, conn.ip):
    mode = UNWRAP
  else:
    mode = PASS

on_frame(frame):
  if mode == UNWRAP:
    out = extract_payload(frame)
    write_raw(out)
  else:
    write_raw(frame)
```
Add tracing tag `compat_mode=unwrap` when active.
anya: Perf estimate? We need microbench: extra copy & JSON parse per token. Might be +1-3ms per token on edge pod for worst case. Add canary at 5% traffic then scale.
simon: Rollout plan: 1) implement edge translator behind feature flag in edge-proxy repo; 2) add telemetry `compat_unwrap_injected`, `parse_errors_pre` and `post`; 3) canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% in us-west; 4) open customer advisory + SDK guidance; 5) schedule enforcement date (90 days) where runtime will require `x-rw-enveloped=1` and close legacy path.
chloe: Also need to update our cache key computation: if translator kicks in we must compute cache key on canonical raw payload (post-unwrap) to ensure cache hits remain stable. Documented in infra-runbook.
jeff: Edge translator must be idempotent: if a new client already receives legacy frames (e.g., request `x-rw-compat=legacy`), translator should be a no-op. Also include a header `x-rw-compat-injected: true` for downstream debugging.
anya: Ops: add rollback triggers: - parse error rate > 0.8% in canary group - p95 tail latency delta > 6ms - dropped-frames > 0.2%
simon: I'll own RFC addendum and decision note. Chloe can own implementation in edge-proxy and perf bench. Jeff will add telemetry & cache-key hooks.
chloe: I'll kick off a staging PR and include a small python shim tool we can publish for customers that want to run a local unwraper for legacy sidecars.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: edge-proxy/compat-unwrap feature branch deployed to staging at 2024-08-05T09:12:04Z :rocket:
simon: Nice. Let's reconvene after staging perf results (48h). We'll aim to retire the edge shim after 12 weeks once SDK adoption passes 95% or customers agree to upgrade.
jeff: Also add an automated email list to owners of the top 30 client_uas that hit unwrap so support can reach out.
anya: One more caution: tests for partial frames. Some clients send half a JSON envelope then close; translator must buffer until full object or timeout to avoid producing truncated tokens. Set timeout 250ms.
simon: Good catch. Ok team, proceed with the temporary edge translator + telemetry + outreach. Long term, we'll keep envelope-only and require capability header. :thumbsup:
